executiveSummary: Overall maritime cyber threat level: HIGH. This assessment reflects confirmed GPS disruption affecting vessels at Fujairah anchorage, an actively exploited SD-WAN orchestrator vulnerability with potential maritime network exposure, ongoing regional attacks on shipping that raise cyber-enabled navigation and communications risk, and a reported port cyber incident under verification. Confirmed navigation disruption: USCG NAVCEN documented multiple recent marine GPS interference cases near Fujairah, UAE, with no constellation anomaly or authorized testing identified; this presents an immediate navigation and safety risk for vessels operating in a critical energy corridor. Government Advisory Actively exploited vulnerability: A critical OS command injection (CVE-2026-16812) in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem was exploited as a zero-day; maritime operators using SD-WAN for vessel, port, or remote connectivity should urgently verify exposure and patch/mitigate. View Article Regional security environment: The IMO condemned renewed attacks on ships in the Red Sea; while kinetic, the environment may elevate risks of communications interference, deception, or cyber-enabled navigation challenges for transiting vessels. Maritime Advisory Port operations: Community reporting indicates a cyber incident impacting North Carolina Ports (Charlotte Inland Port and facilities linked to Wilmington and Morehead City), with limited technical details and low-confidence open-source confirmation at time of writing; operators should validate any operational dependencies on affected nodes. Supporting Report Targeted ICS/OT threat: Reporting attributes four attack waves by Boggy Serpens/MuddyWater against a national marine and energy company (Aug 2025-Feb 2026), using phishing, macros, backdoors, and new payloads-reinforcing persistent interest in maritime-adjacent ICS environments. Threat Intel Assessment notes: • Facts are sourced from the linked articles and advisories. • The elevated threat level is an analytical judgment synthesizing multiple events. • Outlook judgments below reflect current indicators and are not predictions of certainty. Confidence: high for USCG NAVCEN and Arista vulnerability exploitation; medium for IMO context; medium for APT interest; low for the reported NC Ports incident.
